findings.F1: The 5-day move rises step by step with the coin's own 30-day return at an hourly close. On non-overlapping 120-hour cells, the top fifth of 30-day returns is followed by an unusual move of +1.26 % (t 2.95, 1076 cases, strength 0.107) and the fourth fifth by +0.52 % (t 1.29). The three lower fifths are followed by −0.55 %, −0.99 % and −0.67 % (t −1.57, −3.28, −2.14). The t's pool 19 coins over shared dates, so they overstate independence.
findings.F2: The book earns almost only while the coin's 30-day return is high. Its hourly position gain is 1.59 and 1.55 bps in the top two fifths of 30-day return, against 0.15, −0.74 and 0.25 bps in the three lower fifths (about 107,500 position-hours each).
findings.F3: Nearness to the 30-day high carries the move only at the very top. Cells closest to the high (about 2 % below on average) are followed by +1.25 % unusual over 5 days (t 2.86, 1137 cases). The next three fifths give +0.17 %, −0.10 % and −1.33 % (t −4.32, about 27 % below the high), and the farthest fifth gives −0.02 %. The relation is not monotone.

findings.F5: The size of the 24-hour surge, on its own, does not grade the 5-day move. By surge decile the unusual move runs +0.35 %, +0.70 %, −0.03 %, −1.11 %, −1.35 %, −0.15 %, +0.22 %, +0.23 %, −0.33 % and +1.43 % (top decile t 1.90). It is not monotone, which matches the tested idea's t of 1.85.

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's 30-day return at an hourly close, the more its price rises over the next 5 days beyond its usual 5-day return.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold a coin long for days in proportion to how strongly it has risen over the past month, and refuse longs in coins whose month has been flat or falling.
ideas.name: monthly return five-day continuation

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, is positive, the price rises over the next 5 days by more than the coin's usual 5-day return, and the larger the coin's 30-day return at that hour, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would act on hourly upside surges only in proportion to the month's prior rise, and refuse surges that come after a month-long decline.
ideas.name: surge graded by monthly return
